title: Rules and Regulations for Electric Service by Rate Schedule — One Account per Metered Location
content:
**Clause.** Under Electric Service by Rate Schedule a member may hold any number of service accounts, because each metered location — the house, a shop, a grain bin site, each irrigation pivot — is its own service account with its own rate schedule, meter and bill. The cooperative sets no limit on the number of service accounts one member may hold.

**Clause.** Two service accounts are never opened for the same meter number at the same time. A location already held by another member is moved into the new member's name by a transfer, never by opening a second account beside the first.

**Clause.** Every count, balance and history test in the Electric Service by Rate Schedule rules is taken per service account, unless the rule in question names the member's whole portfolio of accounts.

### The clauses applied to common situations (hypothetical)

| Situation | Result under the clauses |
|---|---|
| A farm family holds a home meter, a shop meter and two pivot meters | Four service accounts, each with its own schedule, meter and bill |
| A buyer takes over an energized house whose meter is still in the seller's name | The location is moved by a transfer; no second account is opened on that meter |
| A rule counts returned payments within 12 months | The count is taken on the one service account concerned, not across the member's other meters, unless the rule names the whole portfolio |

### Points of reading

- "Per service account" means per metered location: a history on the member's shop meter does not count on the member's home meter.
- The meter number is the object that may never carry two open accounts at once.
